entityDescription:
RespectUs is a worldwide provider of export control compliance online solutions.
Export Control is the area of legislation that regulates the export, import, transit, brokerage, intangible transfer and technical assistance of controlled goods, software and technology. Those controlled items are prevented, or otherwise restricted (e.g. by the way of a Governmental license), from being sent to destinations where it is perceived the items will be used in a harmful way.
RespectUs will provide a one-stop-shop online platform to ensure the establishment of mechanisms within any company’s daily operational procedures that provide checks and safeguards at vulnerable points of the system. The use of this SaaS (Software-as-a-Service) will reduce the risk of illegal exports, and to be punished by criminal sanctions and important fines.
This one-stop-shop solution will reduce customer pains by offering full automation of screening and checks processes, help in classification of dual-use and other sensitive items, incorporating legislations of all relevant countries and assistance in reaching and proving overall export control compliance. The solution will be used internally by CEOs, compliance officers and product engineers, but also by licensing offices. 
The platform will be composed of different modules, each of them being able to be subscribed to individually: risk assessment, customer screening, product classification, end-use checks, license determination, sanctions & embargoes, knowledge base.

The Institute of Satellite Geodesy and Inertial Sensing of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) is primarily dedicated to the research and development of quantum technologies, quantum sensor technology and innovative quantum metrological solutions for innovative terrestrial and space-based applications, including the realization of prototype solutions.
The primary research goals of the institute include:
- new developments based on innovative quantum technological methods, which will significantly contribute to the solution of societal and technological challenges,
- novel systems of quantum sensors - for example, high-precision inertial sensors - for space and terrestrial applications that make available and exploit the capabilities of the full spectrum of quantum physical and quantum optical insights, and building upon these
- groundbreaking geodetic applications, advanced reference systems in space and time, and quantum-based navigation solutions.

entityDescription:
The Maria Curie-Skłodowska University (UMCS) in Lublin is the largest university in eastern Poland. In the Ranking of Universities, "Perspektywy" ranks high among Polish universities in the category of "employer preferences", and in the Lubelskie Voivodeship, it has been in the first place for years. The University is at the forefront of universities in Poland in terms of the total number of foreign students. Currently, 1,900 foreigners from nearly 50 countries study here. UMCS initiated the Research in Lublin Program, under which, in cooperation with the Lublin City Hall, it conducts activities aimed at acquiring and employing outstanding scientists from abroad.
The university takes part in pro-entrepreneurial initiatives and programs in the Lublin region, participating, inter alia, in the project "Start-up Platforms for new ideas - Eastern Business Accelerator", where it provides specialized services for start-ups, and in the project "Innovation Incubator 2.0", whose task is to support economically useful results of research and development works and their commercialization.
The strength of UMCS is the academic staff and the research they carry out. Years ago, the University became the cradle of Polish optical fibers. Outstanding achievements in this field are achieved by the team of prof. Paweł Mergo. Many employees of the University can be proud of research of a breakthrough for society, ie: the introduction of a preparation increasing the immunity of bees to the Polish market; creation of industrial technology for the production of mutanase; development of a bio-fertilizer that stimulates the sprouting and growth of legumes and an innovative method of asphalt modification. The UMCS also conducts research on the innovative use of the laccase enzyme in the treatment of cervical cancer, and researchers from UMCS and the Medical University of Lublin have jointly developed a preparation of earthworm celomatous fluid, which in vitro destroys lung cancer cells in 75–5 years. 80%. It is worth mentioning the successes of employees conducting research in the field of biophysics, who broke the world record for resolution in infrared microscopy and discovered a new method of molecular imaging.

entityDescription: The Spanish National Research Council (Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Cientificas, CSIC), is the largest public research institution in Spain and the third largest in Europe. CSIC covers all fields of knowledge. The scientific activity of its 70 fully own institutes/centres and 53 joint units with universities or other research institutions is organized around three global areas. The Marine Research Institute (Instituto de Investigaciones Marinas, IIM-CSIC), is a CSIC own institute, develops research on Natural Resources, Agricultural Sciences (which includes Aquaculture) and Food Science & Technology. The overall aim of IIM is contributing to the sustainable development of the extensive fisheries and aquaculture activities off NW Spain and its associated transformation industry. IIM-CSIC has a proven record of experience participating in EU and National R+D+I projects and collaborating with SME of the marine fisheries and aquaculture and food technology sectors. Company description: Ellinogermaniki Agogi (EA) is an educational organization of private law, officially recognized by the state. EA was the first Greek educational organization, which applied Open and Distance Learning in secondary level education in the year of 1993.
Since 1998, the organization has established a devoted department, the Research and Development (R&D) Department for the design, development and implementation of research activities in education, expanding the collaboration with Universities and Research Institutions across Europe. The R&D Department, which currently employs 13 full time researchers, acts as interface between the pedagogical research, the technological innovation and the school community.
Since its foundation, the R&D department has been actively involved in more than 11 European projects dedicated to Astronomy or Space exploration as well as many more which were partly related to these two fields. In 2012 EA worked with ESA’s education department to intergrade ESA’s interactive applications in the Go-Lab(https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/317601)platform. As part of the EU Space Awarenessproject(https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/638653)consortium, EA worked alongside ESA’s education representative and numerous ESERO offices designing and delivering e-learning resources for educators and educational resources for students. Following Space Awareness, EA was also part of the SpaceEU project(https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/821832)in which ESA Education was a member of the advisory board. EA is familiar with ESA’s educational content as it has been making use of them for many years not only internally in the school but also in the framework of EU projects and teacher training courses. EA also has a long experience in designing and organizing teacher training workshops and courses on Astronomy and Space exploration.
The work of the R&D Department also focuses on the following areas:
a) the development of methodologies and empirical research to investigate processes of learning and knowledge acquisition in various subject-matter areas (physics, mathematics, biology, history, etc.);
b) the collaboration with computer science departments and artificial intelligence labs for the development of computational models and AI learning systems;
c) the collaboration with Universities and private companies for the development and testing of educational software;
d) the design of technology-supported learning and e-learning environments.

entityName: Centro Interdisciplinar de Investigação Marinha e Ambiental
entityDescription:
CIIMAR was established in 2000 and mobilises a multidisciplinary, highly skilled and motivated team (474 members, incl. 210 with PhD) that works at the frontier of knowledge and innovation. The CIIMAR mission is to promote transdisciplinary research, technological development, and training, contributing to advances in scientific knowledge and sustainability of the marine and coastal environments. CIIMAR fields of expertise cover three research domains: GLOBAL CHANGES AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, AQUACULTURE AND SEAFOOD QUALITY, and MARINE BIOTECHNOLOGY, addressing important economic and societal challenges and contributing to achieving UN Sustainable Development Goals. To deliver our mission and build a shared understanding and valorisation of the ocean, CIIMAR is strongly involved in partnerships, public engagement, and literacy.
CIIMAR publishes annually about 450 ISI publications (60% Q1), supports over 100 PhD and MSc theses, and participates in relevant European and global knowledge and innovation networks (e.g. MARBEF, EUROMARINE, EPBRS, EATIP, ICES, EOOS, AtlantOS, GEO BON, MBON, European Marine Board). The centre features well-equipped laboratories, technological core platforms, and cultivation and animal experimental facilities approved by the Portuguese Veterinary Authority. CIIMAR integrates research infrastructures of national and European relevance: the European Marine Biological Resource Centre (EMBRC-ERIC), the European Multidisciplinary Seafloor Observatory (EMSO-ERIC), the Microbial Resource Research Infrastructure (MIRRI-PT), and the National Infrastructure for Chemical Biology and Genetics (PT-OPENSCREEN).

entityDescription:
VARIEL has been in the business for over fifty years. In 1964 the manufacturing plant was established as a division of a fastener assembly plant called Montážní podnik spojů Praha (Prague Mounting Joint Venture) in Zruč nad Sázavou. The company satisfied needs for fasteners used in a large scale of packaging and technology sheltering. VARIEL, as a joint-stock company was founded in 1993.
Originally this technology referred to utility sheds only. Till present they have remained a part of the company’s product range in a changed form. In the 80s company expanded its product range and included containers designated for accommodating of various kinds of technological systems which were principally designed for the use in telecommunication constructions. Since the mid-90s the technological and special containers have become leading products in the company’s product range.
At the turn of the century, the product range was expanded to include standardized ISO certified containers that are used primarily in the military and integrated rescue systems, but also in the civilian sphere. In addition to containers, fiberglass and composite products form an important part of our product range, the main market of which is the sector of mass transport vehicle production, especially rail vehicles.
Undoubtedly, Variel´s telephone booths and fiber glass postal boxes have remained our most popular products throughout the Czech Republic.
Variel is located on the outskirts of Zruč nad Sázavou, which is about 60 km southeast of Prague and 5 km far from the motorway D1 (connecting Prague and Brno). The company has its own railway delivery tracks that lead to the company from the nearby railway station.
The company employs approximately 170 employees. In addition to a high degree of know-how, the company also has very modern technological equipment. In its machinery we can find a wide range of very sophisticated CNC machines, e.g. 2D laser for sheet metal burning, 3D laser for profile burning, press brakes, punching machines, double-sided sheet bender, 3D tube bender, 3D printer, five-axis machining center, welding robot specially designed for container welding, modern paint shop with surface preparation by blasting, degreasing and phosphating, welding machines for welding steel, stainless steel and aluminum, top certified workstation for gluing etc.

Company description: VARIEL has been in the business for over fifty years. In 1964 the manufacturing plant was established as a division of a fastener assembly plant called Montážní podnik spojů Praha (Prague Mounting Joint Venture) in Zruč nad Sázavou. The company satisfied needs for fasteners used in a large scale of packaging and technology sheltering. VARIEL, as a joint-stock company was founded in 1993.
Originally this technology referred to utility sheds only. Till present they have remained a part of the company’s product range in a changed form. In the 80s company expanded its product range and included containers designated for accommodating of various kinds of technological systems which were principally designed for the use in telecommunication constructions. Since the mid-90s the technological and special containers have become leading products in the company’s product range.
At the turn of the century, the product range was expanded to include standardized ISO certified containers that are used primarily in the military and integrated rescue systems, but also in the civilian sphere. In addition to containers, fiberglass and composite products form an important part of our product range, the main market of which is the sector of mass transport vehicle production, especially rail vehicles.
Undoubtedly, Variel´s telephone booths and fiber glass postal boxes have remained our most popular products throughout the Czech Republic.
Variel is located on the outskirts of Zruč nad Sázavou, which is about 60 km southeast of Prague and 5 km far from the motorway D1 (connecting Prague and Brno). The company has its own railway delivery tracks that lead to the company from the nearby railway station.
The company employs approximately 170 employees. In addition to a high degree of know-how, the company also has very modern technological equipment. In its machinery we can find a wide range of very sophisticated CNC machines, e.g. 2D laser for sheet metal burning, 3D laser for profile burning, press brakes, punching machines, double-sided sheet bender, 3D tube bender, 3D printer, five-axis machining center, welding robot specially designed for container welding, modern paint shop with surface preparation by blasting, degreasing and phosphating, welding machines for welding steel, stainless steel and aluminum, top certified workstation for gluing etc.

entityDescription:
Climatic warming and the associated increasingly prolonged periods of drought are having a significant impact on our environment. Prolonged periods of drought weaken ecosystems and facilitate the conditions for vegetation fires (forest and field fires) to start and spread in Germany as well. According to the Federal Environment Agency, for example, almost twice as many fires occurred in 2018 and 2019 as in previous years. The risk is expected to increase much more drastically in the future!Settlement structures, infrastructures and our environment are increasingly at risk.
This also poses new challenges for insurance companies, especially in damage and risk management.

At the same time, artificial intelligence methods offer the possibility of using existing data resources to better prepare us for these growing risks.
Using the latest machine learning methods, Karuna Technology's research will leverage existing data from climate models as well as Earth observation satellites to accurately determine and control fire risks.
Karuna Technology is versatilely positioned to solve the problems that arise. Experts from the fields of deep learning and computer vision, key account management in the insurance sector, earth observation, space engineering and business development are part of the team.
For the development of the necessary algorithms, cooperations with renowned scientific institutes are in place. These include the European Space Agency (ESA), the Fraunhofer Institute for Computer Graphics Research, the Senckenberg Natural Research Society and the Technical University of Darmstadt.

in Quebec, Reaction Dynamics (RDX) is developing rockets to provide routine access to earth's orbit. The company addresses the environmental issue of launching satellites to orbit by turning recycled polymers into high-performance rocket fuel.

The company is vertically integrated and is building an eco-friendly launch vehicle featuring a proprietary hybrid propulsion system and can deliver the same payload to orbit as it's competitors for 1/3 of the price while emitting 30% less CO2. It’s one- of-a-kind, patent-pending hybrid propulsion technology enables these affordable launch services, with short lead times.

Its innovative approach solves the persisting issue with hybrid engines: limited performance over long duration burn times. This technology enables affordable, environmentally friendly and reliable launch services that can be rapidly scaled

entityDescription:
PlanAdapt  is an independent global network-based  organisation  that provides knowledge services in support of effective, economically just and socially inclusive climate change adaptation and climate risk management around the world. We approach complex challenges through transdisciplinary mixed methods and engagement of doers and thinkers across the spheres of science, policy and practice. Our advisors and researchers are  specialised  in methods and processes to bridge the adaptation science-action gap. 
 PlanAdapt  focuses on a suite of advisory services that enable innovative and effective adaptation to climate impacts and management of climate-related risks. We are a group of ‘thinkers’, that conduct applied research and develop conceptual approaches for adaptation, and ‘doers’ in sectors and contexts where current and future climate risks matter. This mixture allows us to constantly calibrate our knowledge pool through balancing tacit, experience-based knowledge from our practitioners and explicit knowledge from research and theory.

entityDescription:
The University of Rzeszow, constituted in 2001, is the largest university in the south-east of Poland (Podkarpackie region), educating over 17,000 students in 60 academic disciplines. It consists of 4 colleges: the College of Humanities, the College of Medical Sciences, the College of Natural Sciences, the College of Social Sciences, which are divided into 21 single-disciplinary institutes. 
The University, accredited to offer 18 doctoral and 6 post-doctoral degree studies, is proud of fruitfulcooperation with its stakeholders from both the social and economic environment, including enterprises, industry, central and local governments and other academic centers. Its infrastructure and human resources potential enable not only to create new quality in the area of scientific development, but also in commercial services. University serves as a platform for dialogue, exchange of ideas and creation of new solutions at theoretical and practical levels. Hence, its active participation in projects in the fields of basic and applied sciences. 
Within the College of Natural Sciences there are the following research centres: 
The Centre for Microelectronics and Nanotechnology with laboratories:
- Technological complex: MBE technology with all parameters control (e.g TOF SIMS, HR XRD, SEM, AFM, Raman spectrosopy) with clean room infrastructures
- Photolithography and electron lithography technological laboratory EDX Computer-aided technological measurements laboratory for students
- Student laboratory for conduction phenomena in semi-conduction structures
- Optical phenomena in semi-conductor laboratory for students
- Low-temperature luminescence science laboratory
- Science laboratory for magnetic transportation in nanostructures
The main area of its activity is focused around Quantum heterostructures for photonics and optoelectronics. The Centre realizes application projects from national financial instruments dedicated to heterostructures for IR detectors in wide range of applications from 1.2um up to 12um based on SLS-II type. It develops the technology based on II-VI semiconductors compounds also for IR applications as well as for Thz sources and detectors. The coherent laboratory allows to produce and verify all the necessary properties like crystallographic and chemical quality, structural and electronic properties of surfaces and interfaces. 
The Centre for Innovation and Knowledge Transfer in Technology and Life Sciences with laboratories:
- Industrial Materials Technology Laboratory
- Manufacturing Engineering Laboratory
- Materials Spectroscopy Laboratory
- Mechanical and Electrical Systems Control Laboratory
- Environmental Research and Control Laboratory
- Prognosis, System and Structural Research Laboratory
- Applied IT Systems Laboratory
- Information Society Laboratory
- Applied Mathematics Laboratory
- Supporting Unit.

entityName: United Nations University -Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS)
entityDescription:
The United Nations University (UNU) is the academic arm of the United Nations and acts as a global think tank. The mission of the Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS) is to carry out cutting edge research on risks and adaptation related to environmental hazards and global change. The institute’s research promotes policies and programmes to reduce these risks, while taking into account the interplay between environmental and societal factors.
Research areas include climate change adaptation incorporating insurance-related approaches, environmentally induced migration and social vulnerability, ecosystem services and environmental deterioration processes, models and tools to analyze vulnerability and risks linked to natural hazards, with a focus on urban space and rural-urban interfaces. Research is always conducted with the underlying goal of connecting solutions to development pathways.
Beyond its research mandate, UNU-EHS is actively engaged in education. It offers the joint Master of Science degree programme “The Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security” with the University of Bonn. UNU-EHS also hosts a number of international PhD projects and courses on global issues of environmental risks and sustainable development. The institute is based in Bonn, Germany
